words.sense: gradual loss of people, strength or resources through repeated pressures
misconceptions: Assuming attrition and atrophy mean the same thing whenever both appear relevant.
Ignoring the defining evidence needed for atrophy.

words.sense: weakening or wasting away through prolonged disuse or neglect
misconceptions: Assuming attrition and atrophy mean the same thing whenever both appear relevant.
Ignoring the defining evidence needed for attrition.

semantic_axes.description: Attrition is cumulative loss under continuing pressure; atrophy is deterioration because something is unused or neglected.

edges.boundary_rule: Attrition is cumulative loss under continuing pressure; atrophy is deterioration because something is unused or neglected.

misconceptions.M1: Assuming attrition and atrophy mean the same thing whenever both appear relevant.
misconceptions.M2: Ignoring the defining evidence needed for atrophy.
misconceptions.M3: Ignoring the defining evidence needed for attrition.

chains.frame: Which word best describes the decline in Javed’s volunteer team?

beats.text: Javed’s team lost one helper almost every week as longer work shifts made participation difficult.
beats.decisive_clue: repeated volunteer departures under continuing pressure
beats.reason: Repeated volunteer departures under continuing pressure is the strongest evidence for attrition here.

beats.text: Javed’s team switched from white shirts to bright orange ones, but people kept leaving.
beats.decisive_clue: repeated volunteer departures under continuing pressure; team shirts changed colour does not change that
beats.reason: New team shirts do not alter the pattern of people gradually leaving.

chains.feedback_short: Repeated volunteer departures under continuing pressure still decides; the later detail does not change that.
chains.feedback_deep: Attrition means gradual loss of people, strength or resources through repeated pressures; atrophy means weakening or wasting away through prolonged disuse or neglect. New team shirts do not alter the pattern of people gradually leaving.
chains.contrast_rule: Attrition: members leave one by one; atrophy: ability fades without practice.

hints.attention: Look at the team’s numbers and why they fall.
hints.axis: Attrition is cumulative loss under continuing pressure; atrophy is deterioration because something is unused or neglected.
hints.contrast: Attrition: members leave one by one; atrophy: ability fades without practice.

chains.frame: Which word best describes what happened to Elif’s guitar technique?

beats.text: Elif once changed chords smoothly, but after two years without playing she now fumbles familiar transitions.
beats.decisive_clue: playing ability deteriorated after two years of disuse
beats.reason: Playing ability deteriorated after two years of disuse is the strongest evidence for atrophy here.

beats.text: Even songs she used to play without looking require long pauses between chord changes.
beats.decisive_clue: playing ability deteriorated after two years of disuse; further evidence: previously easy transitions also fail
beats.reason: The extra detail confirms a once-used skill has weakened from lack of practice.

chains.feedback_short: Previously easy transitions also fail confirms the earlier clue: playing ability deteriorated after two years of disuse.
chains.feedback_deep: Attrition means gradual loss of people, strength or resources through repeated pressures; atrophy means weakening or wasting away through prolonged disuse or neglect. The extra detail confirms a once-used skill has weakened from lack of practice.
chains.contrast_rule: Attrition: members leave one by one; atrophy: ability fades without practice.

hints.attention: Look at the period without practice.
hints.axis: Attrition is cumulative loss under continuing pressure; atrophy is deterioration because something is unused or neglected.
hints.contrast: Attrition: members leave one by one; atrophy: ability fades without practice.

chains.frame: Which word best describes what happened to Boris’s savings?

beats.text: Small monthly fees steadily ate into Boris’s savings account for three years.
beats.reason: Repeated charges cumulatively reduced savings is the strongest evidence for attrition here.

beats.text: Each fee was modest, but after thirty-six deductions the account held much less money.
beats.decisive_clue: repeated charges cumulatively reduced savings; further evidence: thirty-six deductions created a large total loss
beats.reason: The accumulation of small, sustained losses is the relevant mechanism.

chains.feedback_short: Thirty-six deductions created a large total loss confirms the earlier clue: repeated charges cumulatively reduced savings.
chains.feedback_deep: Attrition means gradual loss of people, strength or resources through repeated pressures; atrophy means weakening or wasting away through prolonged disuse or neglect. The accumulation of small, sustained losses is the relevant mechanism.
chains.contrast_rule: Attrition: members leave one by one; atrophy: ability fades without practice.

hints.attention: Focus on repeated deductions, not any single one.
hints.axis: Attrition is cumulative loss under continuing pressure; atrophy is deterioration because something is unused or neglected.
hints.contrast: Attrition: members leave one by one; atrophy: ability fades without practice.

chains.frame: Which word best describes what happened to Sakura’s spoken French?

beats.text: Sakura stopped using French after school, and several years later she struggled to form sentences she once spoke easily.
beats.decisive_clue: once-fluent ability faded through years of nonuse
beats.reason: Once-fluent ability faded through years of nonuse is the strongest evidence for atrophy here.

beats.text: Her spoken sentences still contain impressive vocabulary, but she pauses before even the simplest verbs.
beats.decisive_clue: once-fluent ability faded through years of nonuse; impressive vocabulary despite halting speech does not change that
beats.reason: Knowing many words does not undo the loss of speaking fluency through disuse.

chains.feedback_short: Once-fluent ability faded through years of nonuse still decides; the later detail does not change that.
chains.feedback_deep: Attrition means gradual loss of people, strength or resources through repeated pressures; atrophy means weakening or wasting away through prolonged disuse or neglect. Knowing many words does not undo the loss of speaking fluency through disuse.
chains.contrast_rule: Attrition: members leave one by one; atrophy: ability fades without practice.

hints.attention: Distinguish remembered words from practised fluency.
hints.axis: Attrition is cumulative loss under continuing pressure; atrophy is deterioration because something is unused or neglected.
hints.contrast: Attrition: members leave one by one; atrophy: ability fades without practice.

chains.frame: Which word best describes the change in Mateo’s calf muscle?

beats.text: Mateo kept one leg in a brace for seven weeks; afterward, that calf looked much smaller than the other.
beats.decisive_clue: calf muscle shrank after weeks without use
beats.reason: Calf muscle shrank after weeks without use is the strongest evidence for atrophy here.

beats.text: He ate normally throughout the seven weeks, but the same muscle had hardly been used.
beats.decisive_clue: normal meals did not compensate for lack of movement
beats.reason: The muscle became smaller through nonuse, rather than from a series of external losses.

chains.feedback_short: Normal meals did not compensate for lack of movement makes atrophy the better choice.
chains.feedback_deep: Attrition means gradual loss of people, strength or resources through repeated pressures; atrophy means weakening or wasting away through prolonged disuse or neglect. The muscle became smaller through nonuse, rather than from a series of external losses.
chains.contrast_rule: Attrition: members leave one by one; atrophy: ability fades without practice.

hints.attention: Look at what happened while the leg could not move normally.
hints.axis: Attrition is cumulative loss under continuing pressure; atrophy is deterioration because something is unused or neglected.
hints.contrast: Attrition: members leave one by one; atrophy: ability fades without practice.

chains.frame: Which word best describes the decline in Ines’s monthly-pass customers?

beats.text: Ines watched the number of monthly-pass buyers drop a few at a time as successive price rises drove riders away.
beats.decisive_clue: repeated customer losses after successive price rises
beats.reason: Repeated customer losses after successive price rises is the strongest evidence for attrition here.

beats.text: The remaining buyers still used the passes as frequently as before.
beats.decisive_clue: repeated customer losses after successive price rises; unchanged use by remaining customers does not change that
beats.reason: Continued use by the customers left does not undo the gradual losses in their number.

chains.feedback_deep: Attrition means gradual loss of people, strength or resources through repeated pressures; atrophy means weakening or wasting away through prolonged disuse or neglect. Continued use by the customers left does not undo the gradual losses in their number.
chains.contrast_rule: Attrition: members leave one by one; atrophy: ability fades without practice.
